clue.text: Drink outside and attract attention

indicators.note: outside tells us the drink's letters go round the other word

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, a drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ordering a beer while standing outside the pub gets you noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like a verb going with 'outside'; it is the noun, a dark beer, wrapped round the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to be conspicuous, catching everyone's notice.

clue.text: Relationship between matron and nurse

definitions.meaning: a female sibling, a family relation
the senior ward nurse ranks below the matron and above ordinary nurses

explanation.surface: A family tie seems to link a hospital matron and a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals the ward head ranked between matron and staff nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a female sibling and is also the British title of a senior ward nurse.

clue.text: Article badly made — a sort of wreath

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: badly signals that the next word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A badly made item turns out to be a kind of wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges MADE to ADEM. An anadem is a garland for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or chaplet worn on the head.

clue.text: Row following last month's failure

indicators.note: following means the row comes after the month

parts.note: DEC, December, is the year's last month
a row is a line

explanation.surface: After last month's argument, things went downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-off or deterioration is a gradual collapse.

clue.text: A little pause does the trick, and that's not new

indicators.note: a little of the words means only a short stretch inside them is taken

explanation.surface: A brief pause is all it takes, and that's an old trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' takes a few letters from inside 'pause does'.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods are those which have been handled before.

clue.text: The end of a sentence or "time"

definitions.meaning: the full stop that closes a sentence, called so in American usage
a stretch or era of time

explanation.surface: A punctuation mark, or a stretch of time, offered as alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is so named in America, and an era or spell is also so called.

clue.text: He's put out when a point's awarded to the winner

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A loser is annoyed when a point goes to the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'annoyed', but means thrown out of a home; 'point' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who removes a tenant forces them out of the property.

clue.text: A coin — the form is quite rudimentary

indicators.note: form means a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient coin's shape is crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not fully developed, so basic and undeveloped.

clue.text: Increases the underworld watches closely

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld
to tend is to look after closely

explanation.surface: The underworld's interest grows as it watches closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells or expands in size.

clue.text: A person looking for quarters — a toxophilite

parts.note: S and E are compass points, quarters of the compass
a toxophilite is a lover of archery, an archer

explanation.surface: Someone house-hunting turns out to be a keen archer.
explanation.walkthrough: TOXOPHILITE is a rare word for an archery enthusiast; 'quarters' here are compass points, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seeks something is a person on the hunt for it.

clue.text: Heavenly fish!

parts.note: an exclamation of delight at a tasty fish, but read literally it is the pair of fish in the night sky, a constellation and zodiac sign

explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac constellation is pictured as two fish in the sky.

clue.text: This would be a record of course

definitions.text: This would be a record of course

parts.words: This would be a record of course
parts.note: 'of course' seems to mean naturally, but it is a ship's course, logged by the crew

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's journal records the vessel's course and events.

clue.text: The viewer needs it for relaxation

definitions.text: The viewer needs it for relaxation

parts.words: The viewer needs it for relaxation
parts.note: the viewer is the eye itself, which needs its cover lowered to rest

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin covering the eye closes over it during sleep and rest.

clue.text: A window with a vista of the sea

definitions.text: A window with a vista of the sea

parts.words: A window with a vista of the sea
parts.note: sounds like a seafront hotel room, but means the round window in a ship's side

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's round side window naturally looks out over the ocean.

clue.text: Taking it easy, being hurt yet again

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
to sting is to hurt

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break after being injured once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxing or idling is having a rest.

clue.text: Made a resounding comeback

parts.note: sounds like a triumphant return, but describes sound echoing back

explanation.definitionFit: An echoing noise rings and bounces back off surfaces.

clue.text: Driving instructors?

parts.note: sounds like people who teach driving, but means those who drive coaches drawn by horses

explanation.definitionFit: Coach drivers drive carriages; a coach is also an instructor.

clue.text: Struggled, so gained converts

indicators.note: converts means changes form, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: Struggling missionaries still won some converts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for new believers; it is a verb rearranging SO GAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in torment or strain hard is to suffer anguish.

clue.text: Valuable growth for tea blenders

indicators.note: blenders mix things together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tea-blending firm prizes a particular plantation's crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blenders' tells you to mix the letters of GROWTH FOR TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth a great deal is precious or costly.

clue.text: Pull out, having added weight

parts.note: extra means additional
CT, carat, is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone is dropped from the team after putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove something by drawing it from a source.

clue.text: Blunder into someone fastening up a dog

indicators.note: into tells us the blunder goes inside the other word

parts.note: a tier is one who ties
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: Someone tying up a dog makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Timid fellow taking care of a minor

parts.note: C/O is the postal abbreviation for care of
a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A shy man becomes guardian of a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint-hearted person lacking courage.

clue.text: American patriot always surrounded by, soldiers

indicators.note: surrounded by means always is placed inside the soldiers

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers
ever means always

explanation.surface: An American hero is forever ringed by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere rode to warn of British troops in 1775. RE are the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Revere was a hero of the American Revolution.

clue.text: Even mislead a good man, a compulsive worker

parts.note: to con is to deceive or mislead
ST, saint, is the crossword's good man
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A tirelessly working saint is somehow led astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady, unvarying and regular are senses shared by both words.

clue.text: Stand by English poet

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate or stand something

explanation.surface: Readers are urged to stick by an English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke was the English poet of 'The Soldier'; 'Stand' means put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was a First World War versifier.

clue.text: Getting cut-up over nothing, though game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone gets upset over nothing, yet is game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-up' looks like 'upset'; split it as cut + up.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a sport played on horseback.

clue.text: The girl left carrying a book

indicators.note: carrying means the outer pieces hold the next word inside them

parts.note: a girl is a miss

explanation.surface: A girl walks off holding a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic service book of prayers for the Mass.

clue.text: Contribute about a thousand and one will get control

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go around the others

parts.note: to donate is to contribute
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Donors who give enough end up running the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M and I inside DONATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule over or command is to hold the upper hand.

clue.text: Untidy appearance may be due to lack of clothing

indicators.note: the appearance of the word is changed, its letters taking a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scruffy look may be because someone isn't dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' signals a rearrangement of UNTIDY's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nakedness is the state of wearing nothing.

clue.text: Stir a dish of oatmeal

definitions.meaning: stir is slang for prison, and ... is British slang for a prison sentence
oats boiled with water or milk, a breakfast dish

explanation.surface: An instruction to mix a bowl of breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a cooking verb; it is British slang for prison, as is the answer (time served).
explanation.definitionFit: The breakfast is boiled oats, and the same word is British slang for jail time.
